title: Abbott Plans to Spin Off Nutrition Business as Legal Woes Mount

contentHtml:
Bengaluru: Abbott Laboratories cut its 2026 sales growth forecast on Wednesday and said it plans to separate its nutrition business into a publicly traded company, amid costly litigation over its baby formula products.

The ​separation will shed a beleaguered unit behind brands such as Similac infant formula and ​Ensure nutritional drinks, which generated more than $8 billion in sales last year.

Abbott ⁠joins peers, including Johnson & Johnson and Medtronic, that have also announced business separations in recent ​years, as large healthcare companies reshape portfolios to sharpen focus on higher-growth segments.

The nutrition division lost ​a major US government supply contract last year and faced higher manufacturing costs that prompted price increases and hurt demand.

The baby formula business has faced a series of setbacks since a 2022 recall and shutdown of ​Abbott's Sturgis, Michigan, plant that exacerbated a nationwide shortage. The company also faced lawsuits alleging its ​specialized formula for premature infants caused a potentially fatal bowel disease.

CEO Robert Ford struck an upbeat tone on ‌a ⁠post-earnings call, and said outstanding legal disputes were unlikely to delay the separation. "Strategically, over the next decade, there's going to be a lot of segments in this nutrition business ... that are going to be very differentiated and kind of high growth."

The company expects the separation to be ​complete in 2027.

Abbott shares ​fell 4% in ⁠morning trading. The slip was likely due to the "potential for nutrition value creation partially offsetting the moderated underlying business fundamentals," J.P.Morgan analyst Robbie Marcus ​said.

REDUCED FORECAST WEIGHS ON 2027

Abbott now expects 2026 sales growth of ​about 6%, ⁠down from its prior expectation of 6.5% to 7.5%. It tightened its full-year adjusted profit per share forecast range to $5.50 to $5.55 from $5.45 to $5.60.

This was unfavorable to the extent of affecting the company's 2027 ⁠trajectory, ​RBC Capital Markets analyst Au Kendall said.

Third-quarter adjusted profit ​of $1.42 per share was in line with estimates. Revenue came in at $13.01 billion. Analysts on average estimated $13 billion, according to ​data compiled by LSEG.
